accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EYFS statutory framework (2024) ELG Building Relationships (work and play cooperatively and take turns with others), Development Matters (2021) PSED for 3 and 4 year olds (play with one or more other children; help to find solutions to conflicts and rivalries) and the Head Start ELOF social and emotional domain (relationships with other children: cooperative play, turn-taking). The topic evidence (takes turns in a simple game with help, offers a toy, uses my turn and your turn) maps onto the race game, the offer step and the button words. Every share in the lab and items was rechecked: 6 strawberries deal to 3 and 3, 8 biscuits to 4 and 4, 2k grapes to k each.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for 3 to 4 year olds: wanting two goes in a row (race game refuses a second tap of the same player and the prediction offers 'Me again'), believing a shared toy is lost for good (fire truck prediction 'It is gone for good', then the truck visibly travels back), grabbing during someone's turn (a Grab it back button that is refused with 'Wait! It is Kit's go'), not noticing a friend with nothing (offer step rejects friends who already have a toy), and unequal shares feeling fine to the child who has more (the 5 and 1 strawberry prediction, then dealing one each).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagshare models the mechanics of sharing itself: a turn token that swaps after every move, a lent toy that returns on a timer, an offer that only lands on the friend who has none, and dealing one each to equal plates. flagwait is about a queue, a sand timer and asking again; flagplay is parallel versus cooperative play; flagcare is kindness and care. None has turn alternation enforcement, a lend-and-return cycle or equal dealing. The shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The race game only moves the counter whose go it is, so the child discovers the swap rule by doing it; the truck leaves, Kit's bar fills, and the truck comes back before the step says sharing is a turn; the plates refuse two in a row and only finish when the counts match (3 and 3, then 4 and 4), so fairness is seen as equal numbers; sorting six cards rehearses the words and actions. Each idea is done first and named after.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Me again' after your go (the game refuses it), 'It is gone for good' for the lent truck (it returns), and 'Yes, fair' for 5 strawberries against 1 (dealing one each gives 3 and 3). The done message quotes the child's guess through A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: again (you just had a go), none (somebody always goes next), grab (grabbing stops Kit's turn), shout (Kit is only borrowing it), keep (you still have two), hide (hidden toys make nobody happy), more (3 and 1 are not the same), all (Kit gets none), mine (shouting does not get a turn), push (use words). Lab mistakes also name the slip, for example 'That plate just had one. Give the other plate one.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short spoken sentences for a family read-aloud ('I have a go. Then you have a go.') and pass the family kid limit of 5.0 in validate_lessons; the adult text stays under the family adult limit while using the precise early-years terms: personal, social and emotional development, building relationships, early learning goal, cooperative play, turn-taking, reciprocity, turn-based sharing and equal shares.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph carries one concrete idea with an example (my turn and your turn, the truck comes back, offer a toy, one each is fair); the adult paragraphs give the framework statements, the three underlying ideas, four named adult mistakes and the lab outline. Explanation overlap with Waiting for my turn, Playing alongside and together and Everyday Kindness stays under the 12 percent limit.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark: the race lanes fit with both counters and flags visible, the My turn and Your turn, Kit tiles are about 160 by 75 px, the three friend cards and toy tiles are about 100 px wide, the plates and Kind and Not kind boxes are over 150 px wide, and the young-mode buttons under the canvas are large. Nothing is clipped and the labels are readable in both themes.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe reported no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, and every Show me completed. Every canvas drag or tap has a button twin (My turn and Your turn, Kit; Give Kit a turn and Grab it back; Give Pip a toy and the others; One for me and One for Kit; Kind and Not kind) and the canvas aria-label speaks each change, for example '3 for you, 2 for Kit.'
